chunks: As for what was narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in saline marshland, and he said: “There is no harm.” What is meant by this is when there is in it a place upon which the forehead may rest evenly, because the prohibition only concerns sajdah upon the ground of the saline land, since a person cannot properly perform sajdah on it. That which indicates what we have mentioned is what was narrated:

key_terms.السَّبَخَةِ: saline land or marshy salt ground
key_terms.السُّجُودِ: sajdah, the act of prostration in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act under discussion
key_terms.النَّهْيَ: the prohibition referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةُ: the forehead, which must rest properly in sajdah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.مُسْتَوِيًا: level or even, describing the required surface

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid on saline marshland if sajdah can be performed properly?
ai.summary: This text gives a legal ruling regarding salat (prayer) in saline marshy ground. It states that praying there is unobjectionable if there is a level place where the forehead can rest for sajdah, clarifying that the prohibition relates specifically to inability to perform proper prostration.
